transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I guess what brings me in is... my eating has gotten so off lately. Some days I barely get down coffee and a granola bar before a shift at the hospital. Which reminds me, the coffee machine in the breakroom has been broken for like two weeks. Can you believe that? We work twelve-hour shifts, and they expect us to function without decent coffee. I tried bringing my own French press, but someone keeps taking my good beans. Anyway, yeah, my scrubs have been hanging loose on me, and I'm not even trying to lose weight. It's just... I don't know, I used to love the cafeteria's meatloaf on Tuesdays, but now even the smell of it makes me want to just go back to bed. Did you know they changed the recipe? They put these weird little chunks of celery in it now. Who puts celery in meatloaf?
Are you trying to lose weight?

No, no, like I was just saying, I'm really not trying to at all. It's just... my eating is so off. Some days it's literally just that granola bar and whatever coffee I can find before my shift, so the weight is just falling off and my scrubs are hanging loose completely by accident. 

Which, honestly, is really annoying because getting new scrubs from the hospital supply is a total nightmare right now. The laundry service keeps shrinking the medium tops, but the large ones are like wearing a parachute. And the color! They’re supposed to be ceil blue, but half of them look totally washed out and grey now. I tried telling the charge nurse about it, but she’s been so stressed out with the new digital charting system they just rolled out. Have you seen those new tablets they make us carry around on the floor? The screens are so tiny, my thumbs hit two buttons at once every single time I try to log a patient's vitals. It's ridiculous... wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right. No, I'm not on a diet or anything like that.
How much weight would you say you've lost since your eating changed?

I'm not exactly sure, honestly. I don't really weigh myself. But like I said earlier, my scrubs are just hanging off me now. I used to fill out the medium tops perfectly, but now they're so baggy. It's just because my eating is so off, you know? Like, some days I barely get down coffee and a granola bar before a shift. 

Speaking of those granola bars, the vending machine in the lobby is a complete scam. I put two dollars in yesterday for a peanut butter one, and the coil turned just enough to push it to the edge, but it didn't drop! I tried shaking the machine, which I know you're not supposed to do, but I was starving. The security guard, Dave, he just watched me do it and didn't even offer his keys to open it. Dave's been acting weird lately anyway, ever since they changed his schedule to the night shift. He used to be so chatty, but now he just stares at the monitors. I wonder if he's sleeping okay. Night shifts totally ruin your circadian rhythm, I read an article about it in this medical journal someone left in the breakroom... but yeah, I haven't stepped on a scale, I just know my clothes don't fit right anymore because I'm barely eating.
Are you ever afraid of gaining weight?

No, not at all. Like I said, I'm not trying to lose weight, so I wouldn't care if I gained it back. I just don't have the appetite for it. Which is weird, because I used to have a huge appetite. Especially for those cookies they sell in the gift shop down on the first floor. Have you ever had those? They get them delivered fresh from this bakery across town every morning at like, 6 AM. I know because I see the delivery guy when I'm coming in for my early shifts. He drives this really old, beat-up white van that squeaks so loud when he hits the speed bumps in the parking garage. The garage is a whole other issue, honestly. They just raised the employee parking rates again last month, and for what? The elevators are still broken half the time, and the lighting on level three is so dim it feels like a horror movie. I tried bringing it up at the last staff meeting, but the hospital administrator just brushed it off. He's always wearing these really flashy silk ties that look completely out of place... anyway, no, I'm not afraid of gaining weight. I just can't seem to eat much right now.
Do you think you would be upset if you started gaining weight again?

No, honestly, I don't think I'd be upset at all. Like I said, the only reason I'm here, really, what brings me in, is just that my eating has gotten so incredibly off. Some days I barely get down that coffee and a granola bar before my shift, and my scrubs are just hanging loose even though I'm not trying to lose weight. 

I'd probably be relieved if they fit again, to be honest, because having to hike up my scrub pants while I'm trying to help transfer a patient from a bed to a wheelchair is super embarrassing. We have these new wheelchairs, by the way, and they are the absolute worst. The footrests are supposed to swing away, but the latch gets stuck on like, every single one of them. I spent ten minutes yesterday just fighting with this metal lever while Mr. Henderson was waiting to go down to radiology. And radiology is freezing! I don't know why they keep it at arctic temperatures down there. The techs all wear those thick fleece jackets, but they don't let us wear them on the floor because of infection control. Which I get, but still. The infection control nurse, Brenda, she walks around with this little clipboard and just glares at people's fingernails. She actually wrote someone up last week because their polish was chipped. I mean, we're washing our hands constantly, of course the polish is going to chip! The soap they use in the dispensers is so harsh, it smells like industrial cleaner... wait, sorry. No, I wouldn't be upset if I gained it back. I just want my eating to go back to normal.
Do you avoid certain foods because they make you feel unwell or because you just don't feel like eating them?

No, they don't make me sick or anything. I just... I have zero interest in them. Like I keep bringing up, that's really the main reason I'm here, my eating is just completely off. I'm barely managing to get down that coffee and granola bar before my shift, and my scrubs are hanging off me even though I'm not trying to lose weight. I just don't have the drive to eat. 

Speaking of the coffee, though, they actually switched the brand we use in the breakroom recently. It's this super cheap powdered stuff now that comes in these massive silver foil bags. They're totally impossible to open without ripping the side and getting grounds everywhere. Frank, the head janitor, was so mad on Tuesday because someone spilled half a bag over the counter and just left it there. Frank is a really good guy, though. He always asks about my cat when he sees me in the hall. He has three cats himself, all rescues from the shelter downtown. One of them is missing half an ear from some fight before he adopted it. I think he said its name was Barnaby? Or maybe Barnaby was the orange one... they all have these really old-man names. But, uh... yeah. I'm not avoiding food because my stomach hurts or anything. I just don't feel like eating.
Do you think your lack of interest in food is related to your mood or stress levels?

Yeah, I suppose it could be my mood. It's just... most mornings I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling, like the day is already completely ruined before I even put on my badge. 

Speaking of my badge, I actually lost my favorite badge reel last week. It had this little cartoon skeleton on it that glowed in the dark, which the patients always got a kick out of if I was doing rounds early in the morning. I got it at this medical supply expo they held at the convention center downtown a couple of years ago. That convention center is massive, by the way. They have this carpet with these really dizzying geometric patterns in purple and gold. I remember just staring at the carpet while waiting in line for a free tote bag from one of the vendors. The tote bag was complete garbage, honestly, the strap snapped right off after like two days when I was carrying my lunch. I think it was a turkey sandwich... back when I actually bothered to pack a lunch. 

But anyway, since I lost the reel, I had to get a standard plastic clip from HR. HR is up on the fourth floor, and the receptionist there, Susan, she always has this glass bowl of strawberry hard candies on her desk. The ones with the little wrappers that look like actual strawberries? I don't know where she even buys those, I never see them in regular grocery stores. My grandma used to have them in her purse all the time when I was a kid... wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, my mood. Yeah, I just wake up feeling really heavy and hollow before work. So I guess that probably kills whatever appetite I have left.
Do you think there's anything on your mind that's making you not want to eat?

I don't think so. I mean, there's nothing specific on my mind. Just that heavy feeling I mentioned. It's not like I'm worrying about bills or anything, though my car insurance did just go up. 

I got the renewal notice in the mail on Tuesday, and it jumped like forty dollars a month for absolutely no reason. I haven't had a ticket in years. The last time I got pulled over was actually when I was driving back from my cousin's wedding in Ohio. It was raining so hard you couldn't see ten feet in front of the bumper, and the wipers on my old Honda were basically just smearing the water around. I ended up getting a warning because the cop felt bad for me, I think. He was standing out there in the pouring rain with this bright yellow poncho on, and the hood kept blowing back off his head. It looked miserable. He told me to just slow down and get the wipers fixed. I ended up stopping at this tiny gas station off the highway to buy new ones, and the guy working the counter had to come out and help me put them on because the clips were completely rusted shut. We were both soaked by the time we got them on. He wouldn't even take a tip for it. I bought a stale powdered donut and a coffee just to give him some business. The donut was terrible, honestly, it tasted like cardboard... 

Sorry, I'm doing it again. No, I don't have anything specific on my mind making me not want to eat. I just don't want to.
Have you ever had a bad experience with food that might be making you not want to eat now?

No, nothing like that. I haven't gotten food poisoning or choked or anything, if that's what you mean. The last time I was actually sick from food was... gosh, it had to be years ago. I got this chicken salad sandwich from a vending machine in the basement of the hospital. 

Our hospital has this really creepy basement, by the way. It's where they keep all the old, broken equipment that nobody knows what to do with. There are these long hallways with flickering fluorescent lights, and it always smells faintly of bleach and damp cardboard. The vending machine is tucked away in this little alcove near the old freight elevator. The elevator has these heavy metal doors that make this loud, groaning noise whenever they open, which always makes me jump if I'm walking past it alone. Anyway, the chicken salad was definitely a mistake. I should have known better, honestly. The mayonnaise looked kind of separated, you know? Like it had been sitting there for a week. But I was so hungry, and the cafeteria was closed because it was a holiday... Thanksgiving, I think? Yeah, because I remember being annoyed that I had to work Thanksgiving while my sister was hosting dinner. She makes this incredible green bean casserole with the little crispy onions on top. She uses fresh green beans instead of the canned ones, which makes a huge difference. Her husband usually deep-fries a turkey in their backyard, which always makes me nervous because you see those videos online of the oil catching fire... 

But, uh, no. I haven't had any bad experiences with food recently that would make me stop eating. I just don't have the appetite for it.
Do you find that you have no appetite at any specific time of day, or is it more constant throughout the day?

It's pretty much constant, honestly. What brings me in is that my eating has gotten so off that some days I barely get down coffee and a granola bar before a shift, and my scrubs have been hanging loose even though I’m not trying to lose weight. 

I usually get those oats and honey granola bars, the ones that come two to a pouch? They crumble everywhere, though. I made the mistake of eating one in my car last week, and now there are crumbs all over the passenger seat. My car is a mess right now anyway. I really need to take it to the car wash, but the one near my apartment always has this massive line on the weekends. They have this giant spinning brush thing that always sounds like it's going to rip the side mirrors right off the doors. I usually just go for the basic wash, but the guy there always tries to upsell me on the undercarriage spray and the hot wax. He's this older guy, always wears a baseball cap from some minor league team I've never heard of. The Mud Hens, maybe? Or the River Dogs? I don't follow baseball much. My dad used to watch it all the time, though. He had this recliner that he basically lived in during the season... 

Wait, sorry. Yeah, it's just all day. I have no appetite all day, and I'm definitely dropping weight because my scrubs don't fit right anymore.
Do you think your lack of appetite is related to feelings of sadness or depression?

I mean, maybe? Probably. Most mornings I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling, like... like the day is already ruined before I even put on my badge. 

My badge is actually cracked right down the middle, by the way. I caught it in the car door a couple of weeks ago. I was rushing because I was running late, and the wind was blowing so hard it just ripped the door right out of my hand. The lanyard got caught in the latch mechanism. It's one of those retractable ones, you know? I bought it at the hospital gift shop because the one they issued me broke. The gift shop has all this random stuff, like stuffed bears with little stethoscopes and these overpriced greeting cards. I bought a card there once for my coworker's baby shower, but I ended up smudging the ink when I signed it because I used a gel pen. I hate gel pens. They always smear if you're left-handed, which I am. My third-grade teacher tried to make me write with my right hand, actually. She used to tap my knuckles with a ruler if I picked up a pencil with my left. It was a wooden ruler with the metal edge, the kind that really stings...

But, um, anyway. Yeah, I think it's tied to that. That heavy feeling just sort of sits in my stomach, and it makes the thought of eating seem exhausting.
Do you think your lack of appetite is more because of how you're feeling emotionally or because of how your body is feeling physically?

I think it's a mix of both, honestly. The emotional part is definitely there, but my body just feels completely drained, too. Even after a full night in bed, my body feels like I just finished a double shift. And by lunchtime, I’m fighting just to keep my thoughts together. 

I actually used to work double shifts all the time when I first started at the clinic. We were so short-staffed back then. The scheduling coordinator was this woman named Brenda, who had this giant wall calendar covered in different colored sticky notes. It looked like a mosaic or something. She used to color-code everything—blue for nurses, yellow for support staff, pink for time off. She had this weird habit of chewing on the caps of her pens while she worked on it. All her pens had these mangled, chewed-up plastic ends. It was kind of gross, honestly. She retired a few years ago and moved to Florida, I think. Sarasota, maybe? Or Naples. My aunt lives in Naples. She has this condo right on the water, but she complains about the humidity constantly. She says it makes her hair frizz up no matter what product she uses. She tried this expensive keratin treatment once, but it just made her hair look flat and greasy...

But, yeah, sorry. It's physical too. I'm just so exhausted all the time, even when I sleep, so eating just takes too much energy.
Are there any activities you used to enjoy that you've stopped doing because of your lack of energy or interest?

Yeah, quite a bit, actually. I used to go running up in Van Cortlandt Park a lot. It's got those great cross-country trails. I’d take my camera up there too, do some photography. I have this older Nikon DSLR I bought off a guy on Craigslist a few years back. We actually met up at this diner to do the exchange, and he insisted on counting all the twenty-dollar bills twice right there at the counter. He was wearing this incredibly thick wool fisherman's sweater, which was just bizarre because it was the middle of July. You know how the city gets in July? It’s just brutal, especially down in the subway stations. The air gets so thick and stagnant. I hate taking the train in the summer. Someone always leaves a half-eaten sandwich on the seat or something, and it just bakes in the heat. I saw a pigeon eating a slice of pizza on the platform once, just dragging it toward the tracks... 

Oh, and I used to play chess with friends, too. My buddy Mark had this really nice wooden board with those heavy, weighted pieces. 

But now... I don't know. I just tell myself there’s no point in doing any of it. I don't have the drive to go out to the park or set up the board or see anyone. I mostly just end up sitting at home by myself, mindlessly scrolling on my phone, or I just sit there checking my budget spreadsheet over and over again. It's just easier than trying to force myself to do anything else.
Do you find that you no longer enjoy the activities you used to, or is it just that you don't have the energy to do them?

I mean, like I was just saying with the park and the photography and the chess... it's not just the energy. I really just don't enjoy them anymore. I just tell myself there’s no point to any of it. So instead of trying, I mostly just end up sitting at home, scrolling on my phone or staring at my budget spreadsheet. 

I use Excel for the budget, but my laptop is getting so old. The fan makes this incredibly loud whirring noise the second I open any program, like a jet engine taking off. I bought it at Best Buy years ago, and the guy who sold it to me had a name tag that said 'Geoff' with a G. I always thought that was a weird way to spell Jeff. Like Geoffrey, I guess. My uncle's name was Geoffrey, but he went by Geoff. He used to collect vintage license plates. He had his entire garage lined with them, from all fifty states. The Wyoming one was cool, it had a little cowboy on a bucking bronco. I always liked that one. Wyoming seems so empty, you know? Just miles and miles of open space...

But, um, yeah. To answer your question, it's the enjoyment. I just don't feel any pleasure from those things anymore, so I just sit there with my spreadsheet because there's no point in trying to do anything else.
Do you think you would enjoy those activities again if your mood improved?

I don't know. Maybe? It's hard to imagine right now. I keep thinking about how I used to run up in Van Cortlandt Park, take my camera out, play chess with Mark... but now I just tell myself there's no point to any of it. I just sit at home scrolling on my phone or staring at that budget spreadsheet. 

I really need to fix my phone, actually. The screen is cracked right across the middle. I dropped it when I was getting out of my friend Sarah's car last month. Sarah drives this ancient Honda Civic that smells like wet dog because she takes her golden retriever, Buster, everywhere. Buster is huge, like ninety pounds, and he sheds everywhere. I wore black pants in her car once and it was a total disaster. I had to buy one of those lint rollers with the sticky tape, you know? The ones where you have to peel the layer off when it gets full, but sometimes you peel off two layers by mistake and waste a perfectly good sheet. I hate wasting things. My dad was always big on not wasting anything. He used to save the rubber bands from the newspaper delivery and keep them on the doorknob. The doorknob was this old brass thing that was always freezing cold in the winter...

But yeah, I don't know if I'd enjoy those things again. Right now, I just sit at home because there's no point.
Do you think your lack of appetite is more because of how you're feeling inside or because of physical sensations in your body?

I think it's mostly how I'm feeling inside, honestly. It's like... my eating has gotten so off lately. Some days I barely get down coffee and a granola bar before a shift at work. I buy those Nature Valley ones, the oats and honey kind, but they are so crumbly. You take one bite and there are crumbs everywhere. I tried eating one in the breakroom last week and I had to sweep the floor afterward. The broom in the breakroom has this bright yellow handle, which always reminds me of my grandmother's kitchen. She painted her cabinets this awful mustard yellow back in the seventies, and it just stayed that way forever. She had these linoleum floors with a floral pattern that always looked slightly dirty no matter how much you mopped them. She used to use Pine-Sol, the original scent. It smells so strong, almost chemical. I can't stand strong smells anymore. 

But yeah, my scrubs have been hanging loose on me lately, even though I'm definitely not trying to lose weight. I just don't have the desire to eat.
Do you feel distressed by your lack of appetite?

I mean, I guess it bothers me a little? It's just frustrating because, like I said, my eating is just so off. Some days I barely get down that coffee and a granola bar before my shift, and my scrubs are just hanging loose on me now. I'm definitely not trying to lose weight. It's actually kind of annoying because I just bought a new set of scrubs a few months ago. They were the Cherokee brand, you know, the ones with the extra pockets on the cargo pants? I need the pockets for my pens and my notepad. I always use those Pilot G2 pens, the 0.7 millimeter ones. The fine point ones feel too scratchy on the paper, but the 0.7 is just right. The ink flows really smoothly. Although, if you're left-handed, they tend to smudge. My sister is left-handed, and she always complained about getting ink on the side of her hand when we were in school. She used to write with her hand hooked all the way around the top of the paper. It looked so uncomfortable. She ended up becoming an accountant, so she types mostly now anyway. She works for this big firm downtown, on the 42nd floor...

But um, yeah, I'm not trying to lose weight, so it is a little distressing that my clothes don't fit right anymore.
Are you avoiding food because you're worried about gaining weight if you eat normally again?

No, no, not at all. I'm really not trying to lose weight. Like I said, it's just that my eating is so off right now. I just can't seem to manage more than a coffee and maybe a granola bar before my shift. And now my scrubs are all baggy, which is a pain because they're the Cherokee ones. The fabric on those is usually so sturdy, you know? They hold up well in the wash. My washing machine has been making this awful clanking noise during the spin cycle lately, though. I think it's off balance, or maybe one of the shock absorbers is worn out. I watched a YouTube video on how to fix it, but you have to take the whole front panel off. The guy in the video made it look so easy, but he had all the right tools laid out on this pristine workbench. My garage is a total mess right now. I've been meaning to organize it, but I just end up staring at all the boxes. There's a box of my old vinyl records out there... I haven't listened to them in years. 

But yeah, I'm definitely not avoiding food to stay thin or anything. I just don't have the appetite.
Do you think you would start eating more if you knew you wouldn't gain weight?

No, I don't think so, because it really isn't about the weight at all. I know I sound like a broken record, but that's honestly what brought me in here in the first place—my eating has just gotten so completely off. I'm really not trying to lose weight, but I'm still just forcing down that coffee and a granola bar before my shift, and my scrubs are practically falling off me. 

Speaking of the coffee, I usually stop at the Speedway on 4th street to get it on my way in. Their machines are always half broken. You press the button for French Vanilla and regular comes out. And they use those really flimsy paper cups, you know? If you don't grab one of those cardboard sleeves, you'll burn your hand off. I burned my thumb pretty bad on a cup of hot chocolate once when I was a teenager. We were camping up near the lake. The water up there is so clear, but it's freezing cold even in July. My dad used to make us go swimming at six in the morning. He said it built character, but I just remember shivering so hard my teeth hurt. He had this old green Coleman stove we used to boil the water on... 

But yeah, no, knowing I wouldn't gain weight wouldn't change anything, because that's not why I'm not eating.
Do you think your lack of appetite is more related to your emotional state or to how your body physically feels?

I think it's... it's definitely more about my emotional state. It's just this constant, heavy, hollow feeling, you know? Most mornings I wake up and it's like the day is already ruined before I even put on my badge for work. It's just this weight. 

Speaking of my badge, the clip on it broke last week. It's one of those retractable ones, you know, with the string that pulls out so you can swipe the door sensors? The plastic part that snaps over your shirt pocket just snapped right in half. I had to use a safety pin to hold it on for the rest of the shift. Safety pins are so useful, though. My grandmother used to keep a whole jar of them on her sewing table, all different sizes. She had this beautiful old Singer sewing machine, the kind with the cast iron foot pedal. She used to make all her own curtains. They were always these heavy floral patterns that smelled like mothballs. Mothballs are such a strange smell, aren't they? They remind me of the attic in my childhood home. We had this big unfinished attic where we stored all the Christmas decorations. The tree always went up the day after Thanksgiving...

But um, yeah, I think it's the heavy feeling in the mornings that just ruins my appetite. I just don't care about eating when I feel like that.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's lack of interest in eating and significant weight loss are not driven by a fear of gaining weight or body image concerns, which are key characteristics of anorexia nervosa (F50.0). Instead, the patient's symptoms seem to be more closely related to their emotional state, including feelings of sadness, heaviness, and a lack of pleasure in activities they once enjoyed. This presentation is more consistent with other eating disorders (F50.8), which can include a range of eating disturbances not meeting the full criteria for anorexia nervosa, bulimia nervosa, or other specified feeding or eating disorders.
